extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors in combinatorics and theoretical computer science; potential submitters to the journal Combinatorica
extracted.subtask_description: The page is the journal homepage describing the scope, topical emphases, and audience for Combinatorica — useful for authors and readers to judge fit for submission or readership. It outlines the areas of combinatorics and theoretical computer science the journal publishes and the kinds of approaches valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope — combinatorics and theory of computing
rubrics_metrics.description: Combinatorica is an international journal dedicated to publishing research in various areas of combinatorics and the theory of computing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be research papers situated within combinatorics or the theory of computing; suitability is judged by topical fit to these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on general techniques and unifying principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasizes on general techniques and unifying principles in combinatorics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal favors work that develops broadly applicable methods or reveals unifying principles, not merely isolated computations or narrowly scoped examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics — combinatorial structures, optimization, geometry and number theory aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers topics such as combinatorial structures, optimization, and aspects of geometry and number theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers addressing these specific topic areas are within scope; authors should highlight connections to these themes when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic research in combinatorics
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes research on algorithms in combinatorics and related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic contributions (design, analysis, complexity bounds) that relate to combinatorial problems are appropriate; emphasize algorithmic novelty and rigorous analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational complexity theory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work addressing complexity-theoretic aspects of combinatorial problems or techniques is within the journal's remit; clarity about complexity-model and results is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization and explicit construction techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigates randomization and explicit construction in combinatorics and algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both probabilistic (randomized) methods and explicit constructive techniques are valued; highlight whether results are existential/probabilistic or constructive/explicit and their broader applicability.
